description: The National Sports Awards are presented annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to recognize and reward excellence in sports in India. These prestigious awards are conferred by the President of India on National Sports Day (August 29).

sections.title: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award
sections.description: The highest sporting honour of India, formerly known as the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award.

key_concepts.explanation: This award is given for the spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports by a sportsperson over a period of the previous four years.

historical_events.significance: The award was instituted to honor supreme performance in sports and was originally named after the former Prime Minister of India.
The Government of India renamed this prestigious award in honor of the Indian hockey legend, Major Dhyan Chand.

sections.title: Arjuna Award
sections.description: The second-highest sporting honour of India, awarded to recognize outstanding achievement in National sports.

key_concepts.explanation: The award is given to individuals who have displayed consistent good performance over the previous four years, coupled with qualities of leadership, sportsmanship, and a sense of discipline.

historical_events.significance: It is the oldest National Sports Award in India, named after Arjuna, a central character and legendary archer from the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata.

sections.title: Coaching and Lifetime Achievement Awards
sections.description: Major awards established to honor the mentors, coaches, and sports veterans for their lifelong contribution to sports.

key_concepts.explanation: Awarded for outstanding sports coaching. It honors coaches who have successfully trained sportspersons or teams to win medals in prestigious international sporting events.
The highest award for lifetime achievement in sports. It is given to honor sportspersons who have contributed to sports not only through their active career but also after their retirement.
A rolling trophy awarded annually to the university that delivers the overall top performance in inter-university tournaments.

historical_events.significance: Instituted to recognize and elevate the status of sports coaches (Gurus) in India.
Established to honor the lifetime dedication and contribution of veteran athletes to Indian sports.

sections.title: Prize Money and Honours List
sections.description: Details regarding the cash prizes and statuettes/medals given under various National Sports Awards categories.

key_associations.extra_info: The awardee receives a medallion, a certificate, and the cash prize.
The awardee receives a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a certificate, and the cash prize.
The awardee receives a bronze statuette of Guru Dronacharya, a certificate, and the cash prize.
Awarded to coaches who have produced outstanding results in the recent past.
The awardee receives a statuette of Major Dhyan Chand, a certificate, and the cash prize.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts, historical firsts, and superlative data points frequently asked in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: Chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand was the first-ever recipient of the Khel Ratna Award in the year 1991-92.
Shooter Abhinav Bindra remains the youngest sportsperson to win the Khel Ratna Award, receiving it at the age of 18.
Weightlifter Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to receive the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award (1994-95).
Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar became the first cricket player to be honored with the Khel Ratna Award in 1997-98.
National Sports Day is celebrated on August 29 every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of the 'Wizard of Hockey', Major Dhyan Chand.
